A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Advancing Expert Specialization for Better MoE and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations across 11 benchmarks and three MoE models in Table 1, alongside load-balancing, routing, and ablation results in Figures 2–4.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark evaluations and experimental analyses, including the appendix visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C retain the same combined objective, orthogonality and variance losses, expert/router components, and routing procedure.

E1.justification: Both use Numina, GLUE, and FLAN training data and the same 11 evaluation benchmarks covering mathematics, multi-domain tasks, and code generation. No evaluated domain or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains With Aux Loss, Loss-Free Balancing, GShard, and ST-MoE for each model. Figures 2–4 also retain the same loss-combination comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices E–F retain the same three models, six metrics, LoRA configuration, inference settings, and validation procedures. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The load-balancing analysis, expert/routing measurements, and loss ablations in Figures 2–4 are unchanged. Appendix H retains the same PCA visualizations and overlap analysis.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same ± reporting practice and entries. Neither version adds or revises run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical entries match, including Ours at 63.30±0.70 on HumanEval with DeepSeek-MoE-16B. Figures 2–6 and the accompanying reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, gradient derivations, Lemmas 1–2, and their assumptions and proofs in Appendix C.3 are retained without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about specialization, routing diversification, preserved load balance, and improvements of up to 23.79% without architectural changes.

C2.justification: The interpretations of expert/router interactions and experimental outcomes remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same discussion of unexplored visual and multimodal applications, lightweight fine-tuning, and distributed deployment.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix F retain the same hardware, software, hyperparameters, implementation instructions, and inference details. Both retain the future code-release promise without new access instructions for the proposed method.

R1.justification: All 83 references and their substantive use match. Section 5 retains the same positioning relative to auxiliary balancing losses and orthogonality methods.

P1.justification: V2 adds equal-contribution and corresponding-author notes, contact emails, and a NeurIPS 2025 conference footer. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged after matching content across page breaks.

P2.justification: V2 reformats the author block and reflows text and existing displays, including shifting Figures 2–3 vertically and moving the conclusion onto page 10. The same two tables and six figures remain, with unchanged display content.

improvement.justification: V2 adds author-role and contact information and adjusts conference formatting, while retaining the same scientific text, proofs, results, limitations, and reproducibility details. These limited presentation changes do not produce a meaningful overall gain or loss in paper quality.
